```{r}
library(tidyverse)
set.seed(222)
theme_set(theme_bw())
```

Read the data.

```{r}
# All soil core data
soil_cores <- read_csv("data/exide-soil-cores.csv") |>
  filter(pb_ppm <= 5e3)

# Samples from the expanded areas north (ENA) and south (ESA )
ena_esa <- soil_cores |>
  # Create an "area" column
  mutate(area = str_sub(property_id, 1, 3)) |>
  # Keep only the rows in the expanded area
  filter(area %in% c("ENA", "ESA")) |>
  # Slice a smaller sample, so it's easier to visualize
  slice_sample(n = 40, by = area)
```

First, let's visualize the raw data. With a categorical predictor, you can _jitter_ the x-axis so the points don't overlap.

```{r}
ggplot(ena_esa, aes(area, pb_ppm)) +
  geom_point(
    shape = 21,
    fill = "cornflowerblue",
    color = "white",
    alpha = 0.5,
    position = position_jitter(width = 0.15, height = 0, seed = 222)
  )
```

Now, fit the model with `lm()`.

```{r}
# The formula is the same whether the predictor is continuous or
ena_esa_lm <- lm(pb_ppm ~ area, data = ena_esa)
```

Use `summary()` to see the coefficients and other properties of the model.

```{r}
summary(ena_esa_lm)
```

NOTE: we never made the dummy variable. `lm()` does that under the hood for you.
